learning_outcomes.text: Identify the most common machine elements in industrial equipment, know their characteristics and applications.
Select or dimension machine elements for industrial equipment.
Kinematic and dynamic simulation of mechanisms by computer.
Perform kinematic and kinetic analysis of mechanical assemblies, machines and mechanisms using classical and analytical mechanics.
Apply the fundamental laws of classical and analytical mechanics to design cam systems, brakes, clutches and gears.
Perform computer simulations of mechanisms and study their kinematic variables.
Handle laboratory instruments to perform basic design of machine elements, obtaining results and drawing conclusions from them.
Able to work in a team, apply critical reasoning, make decisions, and communicate knowledge and conclusions in the field of mechanical engineering.

syllabus_topics: Kinematic and dynamic analysis of planar and spatial mechanisms
Theory of cams, brakes, clutches, and gears
Synthesis of mechanisms: procedures for mechanism generation
Description of simple articulated mechanisms: four-bar linkage, crank-slider and slider-crank
Graphic methods for the analysis of simple articulated mechanisms: Determination of trajectories
Graphic methods for the analysis of simple articulated mechanisms: Velocity analysis
Graphic methods for the analysis of simple articulated mechanisms: Acceleration analysis
Types of cams, based on the movement of the cam and the follower
Computer Laboratory Practice: Kinematic Simulation of mechanisms
teaching_methods: Classroom presentation of concepts and problem-solving exercises
assessment_rules: Continuous evaluation is based on Control 1 (30%), Control 2 (25%), Control 3 (25%), and Laboratory practices (20%). For the Ordinary and Extraordinary Calls, students who do not pass by continuous evaluation will take a final exam which accounts for 80% of the final grade. The remaining 20% corresponds to the laboratory grade obtained through continuous evaluation.
